es.text: No está el horno para bollos
es.literal: the oven isn't ready for buns
es.meaning: The situation or mood isn't right for something — not the moment to ask, joke, or bring something up.
es.example: No le pidas el coche ahora, que no está el horno para bollos: acaba de perder el trabajo.
es.exampleTranslation: Don't ask him for the car right now — it's not the moment, he just lost his job.

it.meaning: Not the right moment or mood for something. Can be a neutral heads-up or, depending on tone, a sharper warning that someone is genuinely annoyed.
it.example: Non chiedergli niente adesso: non è aria.
it.exampleTranslation: Don't ask him for anything right now — it's not the moment.

bridge.note: Same function, fully different domain. Spanish reaches into the kitchen — the oven isn't at temperature, so don't expect buns. Italian reaches into the atmosphere — the air itself is wrong. Neither image transfers; a learner has to drop the picture entirely and just learn the phrase whole. Register also isn't a flat match: native discussion of 'non è aria' repeatedly describes it as carrying real edge or irritation depending on tone, sharper than a neutral 'not now' — worth a native check on whether 'no está el horno para bollos' carries the same optional bite.

interference.es_to_it: Non è forno per panini or similar literal renderings mean nothing in Italian — the oven image doesn't exist on this side.
interference.it_to_es: No es aire wouldn't be understood as this idiom in Spanish at all.

review.notes: Banked 2026-07-24. Italian side sourced from @learnandloveitalian (Instagram), teacher confirmed native Italian speaker — strong discovery source, formally cited to De Mauro. Spanish side confirmed via RAE's Diccionario del estudiante (rae.es/diccionario-estudiante/horno), which gives the exact example 'no está el horno para bollos' used almost verbatim here. Register flag: multiple native discussions describe 'non è aria' as capable of real edge/irritation, not just neutral timing — this needs a reviewer call on whether that's IT-only or true of the ES side too, and whether the Instagram card's simple 'It's not the right time!' gloss undersells that. Source-authority note: labelled 'RAE (DLE)' per schema constraint, but the page actually checked is RAE's Diccionario del estudiante (rae.es/diccionario-estudiante), not the flagship dle.rae.es — both are official RAE publications, but they are not the same dictionary.

hook.headline: One reaches for the oven. One reaches for the air.
hook.subhead: Completely different image, same warning — don't ask right now.

cue: How do you warn someone it's really not the moment to bring something up?
